task_description: Add a defensive feature: any request that would result in a 404, unless it might have been valid (well-formed image path, or valid-shaped flight-card/event path that just doesn't exist), or is from a logged-in user, or is a standard web file (/.well-known/*, robots.txt, etc.), receives the decoy body 'these are not the droids you are looking for' - except 10% of the time it receives a gzip bomb instead.

verification.summary: Full pytest suite: 590 passed, 5 failed (exactly the 5 documented pre-existing baseline failures - botocore-missing bedrock test, three event_manager async-mock tests, one flaky audit_service append-mode test; no new regressions). The 40 new tests in tests/test_decoy_404.py pass and meaningfully exercise the decoy code paths (exact-byte message assertions, gzip-bomb decompression, all exemption categories, is_exempt_path true/false cases, probabilistic ratio). Docker image builds successfully with the changes (docker build -t flight-card-scanner:decoy-test .). Semantic review: v1 NEEDS_CHANGES (4 non-correctness issues: per-request 50MiB bomb allocation, /admin over-exemption, e2e tests bypassing the real middleware, bomb branch not covered through production entrypoint), all addressed in commit be564c0; v2 APPROVED with 0 issues.
